newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end lower, Dow posts 4th straight loss.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end lower, Dow posts 4th straight loss.

text.p: The Dow industrials endured their fourth straight losing session on Monday, as investors were unable to shake off concerns over an extended rise in interest rates.
The Dow fell 36 points to close at an unofficial 6661, putting the average about 223 points lower than its record high, set four sessions ago on January 21.
Weakest among Dow components was International Business Machines Corp, which fell 5-1/2 to 145. The stock has retreated some 23 points during the last four sessions.
While IBM's loss continued to pace the Dow's decline, the market's focus remained fixed on interest rates, which have steadily crept higher in recent sessions.

The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 20/32, pushing the yield up to 6.94 percent. That left bond yields within striking distance of seven percent, a level not seen since September 23, and high enough to intensify the problems already faced by stocks, analysts said.
"What's significant is that at seven percent, the yield on bonds is clearly competition for stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

Such a development would change the character of the market, which has generally seen stocks move in tandem with bonds. Instead, some strategists are now recommending not only avoiding new investments in stocks, but actually shifting assets in favor of alternatives.
"We've had a whale of a bull market, and from my work it looks like we should have a rest," said John Wosczyna, market strategist at Roney & Co.
"For me, to sell stocks here and buy bonds here is a good decision," Wosczyna said, adding he thought stocks had already peaked or would do so in the next several weeks.

Even though the Dow's decline was narrower than its previous two losses, the performance by the broader market showed signs of deterioration. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by about two-to-one on the New York Stock Exchange, where volume totaled about 440 million shares.
Analysts said concern about a looming economic report -- the monthly employment cost index (ECI) -- also likely contributed to the selling pressure.
"There's rampant fear in the bond market that tomorrow's ECI number is going to be ugly," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
The consensus estimate sees the index rising 0.9 percent but analysts warned a reading of more than 1.0 percent could trigger a sharp decline in bonds and propel rates higher.

"People think this is one report that Alan Greenspan holds dear," Orlando said, referring to the Federal Reserve chairman. Orlando said the financial markets would likely view a big rise in costs as giving the Fed reason to raise rates at its February policy-making meeting.
Among individual issues, shares of Measurex Corp surged 10-1/4 to 34-1/2 after Honeywell Inc agreed to acquire it for $35 per share. Honeywell fell 5/8 to 69-3/8.

After the close, Hilton Hotels Corp announced it was launching a $6.5 billion unsolicited bid for ITT Corp . Hilton said it would pay $55 per share in cash for half ITT's share and follow that with a $55-a-share stock offer for the second half.

ITT shares, which fell 1-1/8 to 42-5/8 in the regular NYSE session, soared 14-3/4 to 58-1/2 in after-hours activity. Hilton shares fell 1/2 to 25-1/4 in the regular session and held steady after the close.

Software Spectrum Inc tumbled 10-1/2 to 23 in the first trading since the company warned late Friday that its third-quarter earnings would fall short of expectations. Early Monday, Piper Jaffray downgraded the shares to market performer from buy.
The S&P 500 index fell 5.50 to 765.02.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 11.02 to 1352.81.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
